claims.statement: The function download exists in app.py.
The download function in app.py concatenates the public directory with the raw file argument.
The download function in app.py has no allowlist for the file argument.
The download function in app.py does not reject .. sequences in the file argument.
The download function in app.py has no post-join containment check to confine served files to the public folder.
Untrusted file query parameter reaches the file sender sink in the download function.
The /download endpoint served by download in app.py requires no login.
Requesting GET /download?file=../app.py returns the running application source code without authentication.

verdict.rationale: Supported claims c4, c5, c6, and c8 show download() joining the raw file parameter to PUBLIC_DIR without an allowlist, '..' rejection, or normalization and passing it to send_file, while c9 shows no authentication. The sandbox test for c10 reproduced GET /download?file=../app.py returning application source without authentication, crossing the public-directory boundary; c1-c3 and c7 remain unverifiable but no key claim was refuted.
